author: potuz
content:
Yes it's mostly about the extra computation. However that should be cached by clients and we suspect there's just still unoptimized paths here. This is the only reason we can't move attestation deadline to 2 seconds at the fork. 

Also in addition after <@703742742135570499> report on the topic. Terence found out that one of the major operators being reorged is because of the combination between timing games and min bid: they play timing games and request bids at the latest, but anyway end up producing locally and they broadcast then themselves. If their blocks have many blobs, they're more likely to be reorged. People should be smarter playing timing games or at least not use a min bid on the first slot if they're playing timing games

author: vladimir_ea
content:
with ePBS the timing of the release of the `SignedBeaconBlock` (and preceding requests for bids from builders) is entirely in the hands of the proposer. 
The incentive for waiting as a proposer is that you will generally receive a higher payment the longer you wait: value of blocks tends to increase as a slot progresses because more transactions become available to include as time goes on, so builders in most cases build blocks of increasing value as the slot proceeds.

author: potuz
content: certainly, the biggest threat here is however the fact that the proposer can release the block later than when the builder has given them a bid. So even if a builder is careful and does not give out trustless bids for requests that come too late, the proposer can still request very early and broadcast late the block with a committing bid for the builder.

author: vladimir_ea
content: yes - but its not clear what they would gain by doing that deliberately? I suppose they could be trying to force the payload to be revealed and not included so they might exploit the transactions? I suppose there might be incentive to do such a thing for a block with a particularly valuable opportunity and the attacker controls 2 consecutive slots.

author: vladimir_ea
content: do you se some incentive for proposers to routinely release the beacon block late?

author: potuz
content: there isn't much incentives to do so from the proposer, and the margins were chosen so that grieving the builder is very hard/impossible. As I said above, if you just release if you have seen 20% of attestations right after the CL block, then only a modified proposer can reorg you (assuming that the block never receives 40% of the votes, and if it does receive 40% then it can't be reorged). If OTOH you wait until 40% then there's reorging that block, the situation of 14899328 which you found is more of an edge case on slot 0 which has to become much better in Gloas, with a reduction of the attestation deadline and the block being propagated being much smaller/faster to validate.

author: potuz
content: yes, the incentives to play timing games do not seem to me to have changed at all

author: potuz
content: which is the reason why I want to reduce the attestation deadline to a minimum viable

hm - perhaps i queried wrong then:
```
WITH first_seen AS (
      SELECT attesting_validator_index AS v,
             beacon_block_root AS root,
             min(propagation_slot_start_diff) AS ms
      FROM read_parquet('https://data.ethpandaops.io/xatu/mainnet/databases/default/libp2p_gossipsub_beacon_attestation/2026/8/1/20.parquet')
      WHERE slot = 14899328 AND propagation_slot_start_diff < 60000
      GROUP BY 1, 2
  ),
  block_votes AS (
      SELECT ms FROM first_seen
      WHERE root = (SELECT root FROM first_seen GROUP BY root ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1)
  )
  SELECT (SELECT ms FROM block_votes ORDER BY ms LIMIT 1 OFFSET 11139) AS ms_40pct_committee,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM block_votes WHERE ms <= 5000) AS block_votes_by_5s,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM block_votes WHERE ms <= 6000) AS block_votes_by_6s,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM block_votes) AS block_votes_total;
```
